extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent proprietors, opponents, and EPO practitioners involved in European patent opposition, limitation and revocation proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practical guidance for filing, conducting, and defending oppositions and for requesting limitation/revocation under the European Patent Convention (EPC), including admissibility, grounds, evidence, amendments, oral proceedings, intervention and third‑party observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file and time limit (Art. 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file an opposition within 9 months of publication of the mention of grant (G 3/97: except the proprietor). A written reasoned statement is required and the opposition fee must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions are post-grant and must be filed within the 9‑month window; ensure fee, written reasons and formal requirements are satisfied at filing to avoid deemed not filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of the notice of opposition (Art. 99(1), Rule 76)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of opposition must meet Art. 99(1) and Rule 76 and, per Rule 76(2)(c), contain a statement of the extent to which the patent is opposed, the grounds relied on, and an indication of the facts and evidence presented in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether the entire patent, particular claims, or embodiments are opposed; identify which grounds under Art. 100 are invoked (at least one ground must be cited, even implicitly); the 'indication' must substantiate the attacks so proprietor and division can understand and respond without undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility/formalities stage criteria (R.79, R.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalities include receipt, copies to proprietor and allocation to an opposition division. An opposition may be deemed filed or deemed not filed depending on compliance (fee in time, fax confirmation, signatures, translations, representative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An opposition will be declared inadmissible if not within 9 months, insufficient identification, no statement of extent, no grounds, or no facts/evidence/arguments as required by R.76(2)(c). Follow Guidelines D‑IV for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition (Art. 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition may be based on: (a) lack of novelty, lack of inventive step, lack of industrial applicability, excluded/excepted subject-matter (Arts. 52–57); (b) insufficient disclosure (Art. 83); (c) amendments added beyond original disclosure (Art. 123(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of clarity or lack of unity are not grounds for opposition. Opponent must cite at least one of the Art.100 grounds (explicitly or implicitly: T 653/99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must indicate the facts and evidence; the indication as a whole must substantiate the attacks. For prior use, the notice must indicate when, where, what and how; detailed evidence may be filed later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late-filed facts/evidence are only exceptionally admitted if prima facie relevant. Opponent should indicate which part of cited documents the opposition is based on. Evidence can nevertheless be produced after the opposition period, but admission is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and composition of the Opposition Division (Art. 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division (chairman, 1st member, legal member if necessary) conducts oral proceedings, communicates with parties, examines the opposition, takes minutes, hears witnesses; chairman has casting vote. No more than one member (not the chairman) may have been involved in grant procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division members have specific roles (1st member does groundwork and issues communications). Check recusal/participation rules to avoid conflict where members were involved in the grant phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural principles: right to be heard and basis for decision (Arts. 113–114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to be heard (Art.113(1)). The decision must be based only on grounds and evidence on which a party had an opportunity to comment (Art.114), though the extent of examination is not restricted to the parties' submissions (EPO may act of its own motion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions may be disregarded. Ensure parties are given opportunity to comment on matters that will affect the decision to respect Art.113/114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings (Art.116 and related rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings may be held at request of a party; rules cover summons, non‑appearance, invitations, final dates for submissions, minutes, language, and recording (Rules 115, 116, 124 and Rule 4 references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare authorisations, handle language requests and late submissions in advance; follow the Code of Conduct for the structure (opening, main phase, decision). Non‑appearance and late filing consequences are governed by the Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking of evidence (Rules 115 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules govern taking of evidence and hearing of witnesses; evidence rules apply during oral proceedings and in the examination stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the formalities for summonsing, witness attendance, and minute‑taking. Evidence may be excluded if late or not prima facie relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by proprietor during opposition (Rule 80; Arts. 52–57, 84, 123)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may amend claims but only to address grounds for opposition (Rule 80). Amendments must comply with EPC substantive requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability Arts.52–57), clarity (Art.84), and must not add matter (Art.123(2)) or extend scope (Art.123(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments cannot be used to 'tidy up and improve the disclosure' (T 127/85). Ensure any amendment is clearly limited to addressing the specific objections raised and stays within original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible decisions and appeal (Art. 101, Art. 106)
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition division may (1) maintain the patent in amended form, (2) reject the opposition, or (3) revoke the patent (Art.101(2) and (3)). Decisions can be final or interlocutory; appeals are available under Art.106. Costs apportionment is governed by Art.104 and printing/translation fees by Rule 82(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appeal strategy and cost apportionment if decision adverse; maintenance in amended form may be interlocutory pending appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention of the assumed infringer (Art. 105)
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may intervene in opposition proceedings after the opposition period if it proves that infringement proceedings against it have been instituted, or it has filed proceedings seeking a ruling of non-infringement following a proprietor's cease request. An admissible intervention is treated as an opposition and the intervener acquires the status and rights of an opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interveners must meet the Implementing Regulations' conditions and will be treated as 'normal' opponents with corresponding procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations (Art. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party may file observations at any time before the EPO; third parties are not parties to the proceedings. Observations are added to the file and are taken into account by the opposition division when proceedings are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations have effect only if proceedings are pending. Use observations to put material on file, but note they do not confer party status or procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for central limitation or revocation by proprietor (Arts. 105a–105c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietor‑initiated central administrative procedure (introduced with EPC 2000) to request limitation or revocation at any time after grant. Pending opposition proceedings take precedence (Art.105a(2)). The procedure is ex parte, designed for rapid processing (<2 months), and the limitation/revocation takes effect ex tunc (Art.68).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must include amended claims limited in scope; the EPO will not examine patentability of the resulting limited patent in this procedure. This procedure avoids non‑permitted 'self‑opposition' (G 9/93).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of examination and EPO powers (Art.114, examination stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: While decisions must be based on matters parties had opportunity to comment on, the EPO's examination is not restricted to the exact facts/arguments/evidence submitted by the parties—examination may extend beyond parties' submissions (own motion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be prepared for the EPO to raise issues of its own motion; however, the parties must still be given opportunity to comment on such issues to satisfy Art.113/114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Late submissions of facts, arguments and evidence may be disregarded; documents filed late during opposition proceedings are only exceptionally admitted if prima facie relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File substantive evidence and arguments within initial deadlines where possible; if filing late, ensure prima facie relevance and indicate the specific document parts relied upon to increase chances of admission.
